messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] color scheme for new logo and shinyStan GUI (a lighter topic)
parts:
We already had the discussion about shinyStan (I objected
to naming it both after Stan and after shiny, but The Nominator
didn't want something obscure or cute [go figure --- he's the
one who gave us "Stan"], like say a riff on "coda" [pun intended]).

"Shiny" is capitalized on their own pages, so I'm not sure
why "shinyStan" was chosen.

I'm OK with changing it --- we've already confused the hell out
of people by calling the R interface "RStan" in print, but "rstan"
as a package and for the repo and capitalizing "STAN" in the first
logo.

As to camel case, a common convention is that classes
are uppercased and variables lowercased initially, so
that'd be "ShinyStan" for a class and "shinyStan" for a variable.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] color scheme for new logo and shinyStan GUI (a lighter topic)
parts:
> On Mar 21, 2015, at 11:54 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Sorry — I thought that was an ongoing conversation.
>
> So given that Inkscape does not embed fonts are
> we good to include both the svg and pngs?

Yes. Anything we distribute outside of the repo
will be either a PDF without embedded fonts (manual),
a PNG (for the web site), and print (t-shirt, etc.),
all of which are OK under the EULA.

We just can't distribute the whole font set as an SVG.
So just make sure we don't have an ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZStan
distributed as an SVG.

Any use as a PDF without embedded fonts, a PNG, or print
is just fine.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] color scheme for new logo and shinyStan GUI (a lighter topic)
parts:
Naming things has never been my forte. 

If it's not a big deal then at this point I would prefer to keep the name shinyStan, although I'm not opposed to changing it if people feel very strongly about it. 

The naming convention for R packages that use Shiny (or add functionality to Shiny) is to use a name of the form shinyX (e.g. shinyAce, shinyBS, shinyIncubator, shinyFiles, shinyGridster, etc.). There are a few exceptions, but none of them use Shiny with a capitalized S.
